summary: The middle hunk correctly fixes the issue by adding Combinable.MOD to the different-type numeric operand block, which is the actual fix needed. However, the first and third hunks each add a duplicate Combinable.MOD to tuples that already contain it — functionally harmless (dict-comprehension keys dedupe) but clearly erroneous and would not be merged as-is.

issues.description: Two of the three added lines are redundant duplicates: Combinable.MOD is appended to connector tuples in the same-type block and the field_type-comprehension block where MOD is ALREADY present. Only the middle insertion (different-type operands) is the real fix. The duplicates pollute the diff and signal a misunderstanding; a maintainer would require their removal before merge.
Duplicate enum entries in a tuple iterated by a dict comprehension are confusing to future readers even though they have no runtime effect (key overwritten with identical value).
